rationale.simple.firstFeedbackMs: Observed 98 to 316 ms (n=4) on the clone. 1 s is about 3 times the slowest observation, leaving room for a cold Worker or Durable Object while staying immediate to the learner.
rationale.simple.resultMs: Observed accepted results took 41.2 to 53.4 s (n=3 product path, n=1 harness); the one-repair run took 53.3 s. One more render and review round adds about 20 to 25 s (render 9.7 to 13.0 s, review 7.1 to 12.3 s), so 75 s covers an accepted result after one repair round with that margin. A result needing more rounds is expected to miss the target, which the qualification report shows rather than hides. n is small: this is a target, not a percentile.
rationale.simple.capabilityGapAnswerMs: Observed 3.3 to 10.3 s for the author's capability-gap answer (n=8, one author call each). 15 s is the slowest observation plus about 50 percent.
rationale.simple.reloadModelCalls: Plan section 3.6: reload/open and local controls make zero model calls. Lane D e2e-r4 save/reload round trip measured 0 model calls and identical pixels; L1 live r1 save/reload returned the identical scene (model calls not counted there). Reload latency itself is not measured here.
rationale.proposalMs and researched/edit: No observation exists, so no number is set (section 3.6 forbids invented targets). They stay unmeasured until a researched or Edit run is recorded.

limits: Samples are tiny (n=1 to 8); medians and tails are not reliable percentiles. Product-path numbers come from one dev clone in one hour; harness numbers use local headless Chromium and include a cold browser per render. Cache state was not controlled: L1 jobs record cache null, and 20 of 21 pilot calls read a cached system prompt prefix (889 to 3051 tokens), so the pilot is warm for that prefix and cold otherwise. Learner approval time is excluded (approvalWaitMs 0 in every simple run).
